newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas slips late, pressured by cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas slips late, pressured by cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures slipped late Tuesday in lackluster trade, undermined by a softer cash and some technical selling when an early move up failed to carry through, industry sources said.
At 1430 EDT, July slipped 1.5 cents to $2.125 per million British thermal units. August was 0.9 cent lower at $2.155.

"Storage buying has provided good support, but if we get too many strong injection weeks, the market may not be able to handle it. I think the risk is more to the downside," said one Houston trader, adding he expected a sizeable weekly stock build in Wednesday's AGA report.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report range from 85 bcf to 110 bcf.
Near-term, most agreed current price levels seemed sustainable, particularly if heat continues to plague some regions.

But while storage buying and pockets of hot weather may underpin prices, traders said sentiment will slowly turn more bearish as stocks climb, particularly if a broader heat wave fails to materialize. Extended forecasts still call for seasonal to below-seasonal weather for most of the nation.

This week above-normal temperatures in the Northeast and upper Midwest should help trigger some cooling demand, but both regions were expected to cool for the weekend and next week. Weather in the the Southeast later this week and next was expected to be mostly normal, while heat was expected to return to the Southwest and southern California next week.
Technical traders still pegged the July range between $2.10 and $2.25, with stronger buying expected at $2.08 and good selling anticipated at $2.37 and the $2.44 contract high.

In the cash, swing gas in the Louisiana Gulf slipped a couple of cents Tuesday to the mid-teens. Oklahoma pipes were down a similar amount to about $2. New York city gate gas was several cents lower in the low-$2.40s despite the heat there.
NYMEX said 20,125 contracts traded at 1420 EDT.
On the KCBT, July slipped two cents to $1.995, while deferreds were steady to two cents lower. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 13.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
